fields.columns: | columns event.time, event.type, site.name, agent.uuid, src.process.storyline.id, src.process.user, src.process.uid, src.process.cmdline, src.ip.address, src.port.number, dst.ip.address, dst.port.number, src.process.parent.cmdline, tgt.process.cmdline
fields.description: Detects usage of the WMI class "Win32_NTEventlogFile" in a potentially suspicious way (delete, backup, change permissions, etc.) from a PowerShell script
fields.name: Potentially Suspicious Call To Win32_NTEventlogFile Class
fields.notes:
- To move around freely without attracting too much attention, attackers often use reliable software (one of the favorites is psexec) that looks normal in an enterprise environment.
- Use the following aggregate to easily group by endpoint: `| group array_agg_distinct(dst.ip.address) by endpoint.name, src.process.cmdline`
fields.query: event.type="Process Creation" and (endpoint.os="windows" and (tgt.process.cmdline contains "Win32_NTEventlogFile" and (tgt.process.cmdline contains ".BackupEventlog(" or tgt.process.cmdline contains ".ChangeSecurityPermissions(" or tgt.process.cmdline contains ".ChangeSecurityPermissionsEx(" or tgt.process.cmdline contains ".ClearEventLog(" or tgt.process.cmdline contains ".Delete(" or tgt.process.cmdline contains ".DeleteEx(" or tgt.process.cmdline contains ".Rename(" or tgt.process.cmdline contains ".TakeOwnerShip(" or tgt.process.cmdline contains ".TakeOwnerShipEx(")))
